newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New South Wales seeks power sale decision in 1997.
newsitem.headline: New South Wales seeks power sale decision in 1997.

text.p: A senior New South Wales minister said on Tuesday he hoped debate on whether to sell off the state's power industry would be resolved by the end of the year.
The ruling Labor Party caucus meets on Tuesday to discuss the sale after Treasurer Michael Egan circulated a paper last Thursday which estimated it would raise up to A$22 billion.

"I said then that I expected a fiery debate, but I certainly don't think the issue is going to be resolved this week, or next week, or this month or next month," Egan told Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio.
"I hope it's (resolved) this year," he said.
Egan said be believed the case for a sale was "compelling".

The discussion paper outlines the sale of seven power stations, six distributors, the state's high voltage transmission lines and the remaining 58 percent it holds in the Snowy Mountain Hydroelectric Authority.
The proposal faces opposition from the Left of the Labor Party, which is committed to public ownership, and from power industry trade unions.
